name: Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome with Mitochondrial Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for congenital myasthenic syndromes with mitochondrial involvement

criteria.description: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with early onset
Electromyography showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes affecting neuromuscular transmission and mitochondrial function
Muscle biopsy demonstrating mitochondrial abnormalities such as ragged-red fibers or cytochrome c oxidase deficiency
Improvement with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors or other CMS therapies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical presentation, electrophysiology, and genetic testing) must be met for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Muscle biopsy and treatment response are supportive but not mandatory.

searchTerms: muscle weakness that worsens with use
drooping eyelid that varies in severity
partial or complete eye muscle paralysis
weakness or paralysis of eye muscles

common.symptomName: Dysphagia due to bulbar muscle weakness
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing from throat muscle weakness
swallowing problems due to weak throat muscles
breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to muscle weakness

common.symptomName: Mild skeletal deformities such as scoliosis
searchTerms: mild bone or spine deformities like scoliosis
eyelid droop that worsens with tiredness
painful muscle spasms in arms or legs

rare.symptomName: Ptosis with ophthalmoplegia mimicking mitochondrial myopathy
searchTerms: drooping eyelid with eye muscle paralysis resembling mitochondrial disease
ptosis and ophthalmoplegia mimicking other muscle disorders
eye muscle weakness similar to mitochondrial myopathy

laboratory: Elevated serum lactate levels indicating mitochondrial dysfunction
Normal or mildly elevated creatine kinase
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective muscle involvement
Brain MRI may show nonspecific changes related to mitochondrial disease
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes encoding neuromuscular junction proteins combined with mitochondrial gene mutations
other: Muscle biopsy showing mitochondrial abnormalities (ragged-red fibers, COX deficiency)
Electrophysiological studies with decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of mitochondrial abnormalities on muscle biopsy
Genetic mutations limited to neuromuscular junction genes
Predominant mitochondrial dysfunction without neuromuscular junction transmission defects

redFlags: Severe bulbar weakness causing aspiration risk
Early onset severe muscle weakness with mitochondrial abnormalities
references: Engel AG, et al. Congenital myasthenic syndromes: pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment. Lancet Neurol. 2015.
